prose: Moses is one of the most foundational figures in the Old Testament: the deliverer of the Israelites, the lawgiver of the Pentateuch, the prophet who climbed Mount Sinai. The symbolism around him has been studied for centuries, and there are layers most modern readers never encounter.

In this episode, Chance and co-host Dylan Saccoccio return from hiatus with a fresh look at Moses, building on the research of Reverend Robert Taylor and tracing the threads through Josephus, Philo, Higgins, and the wider ancient world.

In this session: the meaning of the name Moses and its possible Egyptian and Greek roots, the symbolism of the infant placed in a basket on the river, the Ark motif across world mythologies, the etymology connecting Moses to water, rivers, and the muses, the parallels between Moses and Bacchus, Oceanus as the primal waters encircling creation, and the early church writings that connect these layers.
